architecture.runtime_volume: The live ARaftSimWaterSurfaceActor now owns Zambezi gameplay rendering. Its non-colliding volume core is triangulated only through solver-sampled wet cells and uses the shared raft-transmitting water parent through a Zambezi-local material instance.
architecture.runtime_detail: The live Default Lit surface remains as a 0.035 calm / 0.16 active coverage hydraulic-detail skin. A first-party Zambezi flow normal supplies sub-grid breakup; a first-party foam-lace mask is multiplied by solver foam and speed channels and cannot paint whitewater into calm or dry cells.
architecture.capture_water: The prior opaque Zambezi physical-corridor ribbon remains available for deterministic editor review but is tagged RaftSimCaptureOnlyStaticWater and hidden during gameplay.
architecture.authority_boundary: All new textures, material parameters, smoothing, and opacity coefficients are render-only. Cooked depth, velocity, wet/dry, curved river stationing, bathymetry, collision, buoyancy, raft forces, rapid detection, and scoring remain unchanged.

fixed_camera_comparison.method: Matched 1280x720 offscreen gameplay captures at the same saved-map launch transform, three-second crew command timing, camera offsets, lighting, and scalability. RGB means are descriptive measurements over rows 270-719; the full-frame mean absolute channel delta is in 0-255 sRGB.
fixed_camera_comparison.verdict: Retain as a material gameplay-water improvement. The uniform opaque gray foreground is replaced by bank-clipped olive sediment water with continuous highlights, live relief, and readable raft/crew silhouettes. Coarse 30 m terrain, barren near wall, synthetic vegetation, excessive launch glare, limited crest geometry, and unvalidated hydraulics keep photoreal acceptance closed.

remaining_photoreal_defects: The GLO-30 terrain is too coarse for lifelike Batoka cliff profiles, bank breaklines, talus, ledges, erosion cuts, and rapid-scale rocks.
The near left wall remains largely barren and visibly tessellated; procedural vegetation is repetitive and has no approved exact-species ecology claim.

Launch lighting produces a large smooth glare patch and the water still lacks convincing volumetric suspended sediment, caustics, crest thickness, rollers, holes, spray, mist, and rock-contact plumes.
The procedural field has live breaking structure but is not calibrated rapid-specific Zambezi hydraulics or surveyed bathymetry.
Raft, crew, equipment, animation, contact, and complete-run visual acceptance remain open.
